entry_point.discipline_context: Use equilibrium and curvature as bounded bridges to objective minimisation and numerical relaxation.
entry_point.rationale: The learner knows potential energy, vectors, matrices, eigenvalues, and Python but not formal convex optimisation.
entry_point.analogy_boundary: An optimisation objective may be abstract rather than physical energy, and an algorithmic iteration is not necessarily physical time evolution.

conditional_item_decisions.rationale: Exact line search is explicitly required in the fixed scope.
Armijo backtracking is explicitly required in the fixed scope.
Heavy Ball is explicitly required in the fixed scope.
The quadratic Heavy Ball parameter result is explicitly required.
The specified NAG recurrence is explicitly required.
The convex NAG rate is explicitly required.
The finite-sum stochastic model is explicitly required.
SGD and its constant-step error floor are explicitly required.
AdaGrad is explicitly required despite introductory scope.
RMSProp is explicitly required despite introductory scope.
Adam is explicitly required despite introductory scope.
Newton's linear-system step is explicitly required.
Newton local convergence conditions are explicitly required.
BFGS vectors and secant equation are explicitly required.
BFGS update, curvature, direction, and line search are explicitly required.

chapter_sequence.title: Objectives, stationarity, and curvature
chapter_sequence.purpose: Define unconstrained optimisation and distinguish necessary from sufficient local conditions.

chapter_sequence.title: Smoothness, convexity, and conditioning
chapter_sequence.purpose: Build the inequalities and Hessian language used by convergence results.

chapter_sequence.title: Gradient descent and step selection
chapter_sequence.purpose: Present GD, constant steps, exact line search, and Armijo backtracking.

chapter_sequence.title: Rates, momentum, and acceleration
chapter_sequence.purpose: State convex and strongly convex GD bounds, Heavy Ball, and NAG.

chapter_sequence.title: Stochastic and adaptive first-order methods
chapter_sequence.purpose: Model stochastic gradients and introduce SGD, Robbins-Monro, AdaGrad, RMSProp, and Adam.

chapter_sequence.title: Second-order and quasi-Newton updates
chapter_sequence.purpose: Connect local quadratic models to Newton and BFGS implementations.

chapter_sequence.title: Exercises and worked solutions
chapter_sequence.purpose: Assess theorem scope, a hand update, and Python diagnosis after instruction.

implementation_strategy: Use NumPy-style element-wise operations and an executable one-dimensional gradient-descent diagnostic to make each mathematical operation visible in code.
assessment_strategy: Use exactly three worked exercises: a contract-bound theorem-scope check, a deterministic hand calculation with objective-gradient consistency, and a code diagnostic with separate incorrect and corrected executions.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Distinguish stationarity, second-order local tests, and the assumptions attached to convergence rates.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Classify whether a stationary equilibrium-like design point is certified as a local minimum or only a candidate.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Compute one gradient-descent update and verify the stated gradient from its objective.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Relax a two-parameter quadratic surrogate for a mechanical design objective.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Identify a reversed gradient sign and connect corrected Python operations to the GD recurrence.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Diagnose a numerical relaxation routine for a scalar stiffness-calibration objective.
